**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination — lumbar fusion (CPT 22612)**

- **Member:** Quinn Foster
- **Member ID:** W310107367
- **Reference number:** POC-D89C6A76F0-15779
- **Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-05
- **Plan:** HMSA (Hawaii Medical Service Association), Commercial/ACA, State of Hawaii
- **Governing policy:** *2025 Evolent Clinical Guidelines for Medical Necessity Review – HMSA Musculoskeletal Surgery Guidelines*, https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2025-07/2025%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines%20-%20HMSA%20FINAL%20eff%20070125.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing HMSA's denial of the lumbar fusion (CPT 22612) requested for me by my surgeon, Dr. Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated 2026-08-05 states that the request was denied because the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure.

I am asking HMSA to reconsider that decision. My reason is simple: when I read the plan's own published criteria for this surgery alongside my medical records, the records appear to contain exactly what the criteria describe — including the imaging. This appeal is submitted within the appeal period stated in my notice, which says my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-02-01**. I am sending it in writing to HMSA Member Advocacy & Appeals at the mailing address and fax numbers above, and I am keeping a copy of this letter and its enclosures.

## The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

Below I quote the criteria from the governing policy named above and place my documented findings next to each one.

**1. Symptom duration and impact on daily activities.** The policy states:

> "Lumbar back pain, neurogenic claudication, and/or radicular leg pain without sensory or motor deficit that impairs daily activities for at least 6 months"

My records document 18 months of progressive pain in my lower back and legs, unrelieved by rest — well beyond the six months the plan describes. My function is documented as follows: I cannot stand or walk more than 10 minutes before leg pain and heaviness force me to stop, and sitting relieves it. My examination documents neurogenic claudication, diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes, and no bowel or bladder dysfunction. I am stating my findings exactly as my chart states them so that HMSA can apply its own criteria to them. If the presence of a sensory finding is the basis on which HMSA applied this particular line rather than another, I ask HMSA to say so in its reconsideration.

**2. Failure of conservative treatment.** The policy states:

> "Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months"

My records document supervised physical therapy including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility for **12 weeks**, from 2026-03-23 to 2026-06-15, with **18 visits completed**, recorded in my physical therapy discharge note. That is twice the minimum duration the plan sets, and it occurred within the six months before the request. In addition, my records document NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-20 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.

The policy also allows this element to be satisfied by:

> "Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment; OR"

> "Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment; OR"

My records address both: I completed a full course of supervised therapy and my pain is documented as **progressive** over 18 months and unrelieved by rest. I note for completeness that the policy states:

> "Closure of medical or therapy offices, patient inconvenience, or noncompliance without explanation does not constitute “inability to complete” treatment."

That exclusion does not apply to me. I completed my prescribed course of therapy — 18 visits over 12 weeks — so there is no question of an incomplete or excused course of treatment here. For the same reason, I am not relying on:

> "Documentation of a medical reason the member is unable to participate in treatment"

**3. Imaging — the stated reason for the denial.** The policy states:

> "Imaging studies corresponding to the clinical findings"

This is the criterion the denial turns on, and it is the one my records speak to most directly. My imaging of 2026-06-15 included an MRI of the lumbar spine **and** flexion-extension radiographs. Those studies document:

- grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5,
- 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension, and
- severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina.

Those findings correspond to my clinical findings. My documented neurogenic claudication and inability to stand or walk more than 10 minutes, relieved by sitting, are the symptoms one would expect with severe central stenosis at L4-L5; my documented diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes is at the level the imaging identifies. The imaging and the examination point to the same level and the same problem. The plan's criterion asks for correspondence between imaging and clinical findings, and I respectfully submit that my record is exactly that.

**4. A qualifying clinical condition.** The policy states:

> "At least ONE of the following clinical conditions:"

Among the conditions the policy lists are:

> "Spondylolisthesis (neural arch defect - spondylolytic spondylolisthesis, degenerative spondylolisthesis, and congenital unilateral neural arch hypoplasia)"

> "Evidence of segmental instability - Excessive motion, as in degenerative spondylolisthesis, segmental instability, and surgically induced segmental instability"

My imaging documents **grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5** — named in the first of these — and **5 mm of translation on flexion-extension**, which is motion measured on the exact study type used to assess instability. The policy requires at least one qualifying condition; my records document a diagnosis that appears by name in the plan's own list.

**5. Criteria that do not apply to my case.** I want to be precise about which pathway my request falls under, because several of the plan's conditions are aimed at different clinical situations:

> "Chronic low back pain or degenerative disc disease (disc degeneration without significant neurological compression presenting with low back pain) must have failed at least 6 months of appropriate active non-operative treatment (completion of a comprehensive cognitive-behavioral rehabilitation program is mandatory) and must be evaluated on a case-by- case basis"

By its own wording, this condition describes disc degeneration *without* significant neurological compression presenting with low back pain. My imaging documents severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina, so this is not the category my request falls into, and the additional requirement attached to it is not the applicable standard for me.

> "Progressive nerve compression resulting in an acute neurologic deficit (motor) AND"

> "One of the aforementioned clinical conditions, except chronic low back pain or degenerative disc disease. The neurological deficits must be significant: 0-2/5 on the motor function scale for L5 or S1 roots OR 0-3/5 for L3 or L4 roots. Lesser degrees of motor dysfunction may resolve with conservative treatment and are not considered an indication for early surgery."

This is the plan's separate pathway for an acute **motor** deficit, and the motor-strength thresholds it states belong to that pathway. My records do not describe a motor deficit, and I am not claiming one. I am relying on the spondylolisthesis and segmental-instability conditions above, together with documented symptom duration, failed conservative care, and corresponding imaging.

> "Fusion for the treatment of spinal tumor, cancer, or infection"

> "Revision surgery for failed previous operation(s) for pseudoarthrosis at the same level at least 9-12 months from prior surgery if significant functional gains are anticipated"

Neither of these describes my situation; I list them only to show which condition in the plan's list I am relying on.

**A note on the policy text I have.** The excerpts above are the portions of the guidelines available to me. The policy introduces its clinical conditions with a list, and it is possible the full document contains further conditions or definitions that are not reproduced here — including the definition marked by the asterisk in "conservative treatment*." I have not quoted, and cannot quote, policy language I have not seen, and I have not assumed any threshold the plan has not stated. If HMSA applied a specific requirement, threshold, or definition that I have not addressed, I ask HMSA to identify in writing the exact criterion it applied and the record it found lacking, so I can respond to it directly.

## Additional documented facts in my record

My records also state that I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

## What I am requesting

I respectfully ask HMSA to:

1. Overturn the denial dated 2026-08-05 (reference POC-D89C6A76F0-15779) and authorize the lumbar fusion, CPT 22612, as requested by Dr. Okafor;
2. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician reviewer with experience in spine surgery who has not previously reviewed this request;
3. Review the complete record submitted with the prior authorization — including the MRI and flexion-extension radiographs of 2026-06-15, the physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-03-23 to 2026-06-15, and my surgeon's documentation that this procedure is needed; and
4. If the denial is maintained, provide me with the specific criterion relied upon, the clinical rationale, the credentials of the reviewer, a free copy of the medical policy and any internal criteria used, and written instructions for further appeal, including external review.

I have also enclosed the items listed below. Please let me know if any additional records would help, and I will obtain them promptly.

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-05
- MRI lumbar spine and flexion-extension radiograph reports, 2026-06-15
- Physical therapy discharge note (18 visits, 2026-03-23 to 2026-06-15)
- Office notes and operative request from Dr. Okafor, MD
- [Any additional records or letters you wish to enclose]

Thank you for taking a second look at this. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed, and I am asking HMSA to weigh my records against the plan's own published criteria.

Sincerely,

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
**Quinn Foster**
